Build automation and tooling that improve code quality, testing, documentation, traceability, and software development workflows.
Collaborate on software architecture, system integration, code reviews, and CI/CD initiatives across robotic software and cloud-based systems.

Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or a Bachelor's degree with 5+ years of industry experience.
Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++ with experience developing production quality software applications.
Hands on experience with Generative AI, machine learning, large language models, AI agents, or related technologies.
Knowledge of software development lifecycle processes, Agile methodologies, and modern software engineering practices.
Strong analytical thinking, problem solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
Preferred experience with Azure OpenAI, cloud AI platforms, DevOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, robotics, healthcare technologies, or regulated software environments.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist - AI & Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Brief Description

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Harbor Health is a Texas-based payvider: one company that delivers care and stands behind the health plan that pays for it. Founded in Austin in 2022, Harbor has grown from two clinics into a primary and specialty care network spanning Austin, Dallas, San Antonio, El Paso, and Houston. Harbor pairs its clinics with its own health plan so members get coordinated primary and specialty care, no-deductible plans, and $0 specialist visits when referred by a Harbor clinician. We're building the infrastructure behind that model — the finance, actuarial, and operations functions that let care and coverage work as one system instead of two. If you're ready to help us build a better healthcare system in Texas, we'd love for you to bring your talents to our team!

Position Overview

Harbor Health runs a health plan and a medical group, so a model here can change what a clinician does for a member and what the health plan pays for it. We are hiring Staff Data Scientists to own a machine learning or AI system full-time, from design through daily use.

Right now there are two areas. One is an AI system we are building to recommend next steps to care teams, with large language models and agentic workflows, moving from a working prototype to something clinicians rely on. The other is the prediction models behind pricing, underwriting and care, which need a second look, clear quality bars and steady improvement. Neither is finished, and both affect what a member receives or what the health plan pays. We hire for this role on an ongoing basis, and the same kind of person will be needed in other parts of the business over time.

Position Duties & Responsibilities

Build AI agentic systems and production-grade machine learning models that become core data science assets for Harbor.
Own each one end to end, from the data and definitions to the model, its deployment and its use, and stay with it until you can show what it changed.
Work with clinicians and with engineering and product teams so each one is developed and deployed safely and efficiently, and make the build-versus-buy calls with them.
Set the quality bar: the metrics, validation and release checks that tell everyone when a model or an agent can be trusted, and when it cannot.
Set the roadmap and stay close to the leaders who depend on it. Disagree with them when the evidence points elsewhere, and leave with a decision or a test that settles it.
Make other data scientists better: mentor senior data scientists and raise the review bar.
Use AI in your daily work, efficiently and responsibly, and share what works with the team.

Desired Professional Skills & Experience

Deep expertise in machine learning or AI systems, shown by work that is in use today. That may be large language models and agentic workflows, or predictive modeling on messy real-world data.
You carry a whole system without day-to-day direction and keep your manager informed of everything happening in it, not only the modeling.
Daily fluency with AI agentic development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. You verify, test and challenge what agents and models produce, and build repeatable workflows that others on the team adopt.
Sound evaluation judgment: you know how wrong an answer could be. You choose the metric that fits the decision and name the risk it hides, such as a model that scores well while underestimating cost.
Typically 8+ years of hands-on data science, machine learning or applied statistics, with strong Python and SQL. We work in Snowflake and dbt; experience on any modern cloud data platform transfers.
A bachelor's degree in a quantitative field or equivalent experience. An advanced degree is a plus.

Preferred

Relevant healthcare experience is preferred, not required. Any of these helps:

Putting a machine learning or language model system into clinical use, with its users in the feedback loop.
Health plan, provider or value-based care work with claims, eligibility or clinical data, or building tools with physicians and care teams.
Prediction works on cost, utilization or risk, including risk adjustment (HHS-HCC, RAF) and pricing.

If you come from outside healthcare, for example insurance, credit or applied machine learning, and have solved comparable problems, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

Annual bonus eligibility
Comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits
401(k) with company match
Generous PTO and paid holidays
Professional development and growth opportunities

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Harbor Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: AI/ML Architect - Principal (US - EAST)
jobs.description:
AI/ML Architect – Principal
  **** Please note: This role is not eligible for 100% remote work. Employees must live within a commutable distance of a Slalom Office and must be willing to be onsite at the client and/or Slalom office when needed up to 3 days a week. ****

Who You’ll Work With
At Slalom, we co-create modern technology and software products with clients who are accelerating their digital transformation journeys. We blend design, product engineering, analytics, automation, and AI-native delivery to build intelligent products and platforms that can operate safely at enterprise scale. As an AI/ML Architect, you’ll design and deliver production-grade AI systems that combine machine learning, generative AI, agentic workflows, modern data platforms, and cloud-native engineering across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. You’ll partner with clients to shape strategy, define secure and governed architectures, and move AI solutions from experimentation into reliable business operations.
What You’ll Do
Architect and deliver enterprise-scale AI systems spanning data products, retrieval pipelines, model orchestration, agentic workflows, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, optimization, and lifecycle management.
Design secure, scalable, cloud-native and hybrid architectures across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, including modern AI platform services such as Amazon Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI, and enterprise data platforms.
Lead applied AI solution design across generative AI, agentic AI, multimodal AI, advanced RAG, knowledge assistants, prediction, optimization, computer vision, and decision-support use cases.
Enable production GenAI and agentic AI adoption, including advanced RAG, tool/function calling, structured outputs, workflow orchestration, model routing, prompt and context engineering, memory patterns, and human-in-the-loop controls.
Define AI evaluation, observability, and reliability patterns, including offline test sets, automated evals, tracing, hallucination detection, quality scoring, latency/cost monitoring, feedback loops, and regression testing.
Champion Responsible AI and AI security practices, including governance, explainability, privacy, bias mitigation, guardrails, data protection, threat modeling, access controls, auditability, and compliance-by-design.
Evaluate emerging models, platforms, frameworks, standards, and deployment patterns, providing practical recommendations based on use case fit, enterprise readiness, cost, risk, and operational complexity.
Lead and mentor cross-functional delivery teams of data engineers, AI engineers, ML engineers, software engineers, architects, and consultants, ensuring on-time, high-quality outcomes.
Support business development through proposals, client pitches, solution accelerators, reference architectures, technical points of view, and thought leadership.
Coach and mentor junior consultants, fostering a culture of continuous learning, engineering discipline, responsible innovation, and practical AI adoption across the AI/ML practice.

What You’ll Bring
6+ years of experience implementing ML/AI solutions in production, including classical ML, deep learning, generative AI, or agentic AI systems.
3+ years of experience in professional consulting or IT services, with proven ability to lead client-facing technical engagements.

Hands-on experience designing production AI systems that combine models, data, retrieval, orchestration, APIs, security controls, observability, and user experience into an end-to-end architecture.
Deep understanding of modern GenAI patterns, including advanced RAG, embeddings, vector and hybrid search, re-ranking, knowledge graphs, tool/function calling, structured outputs, context engineering, and multimodal inputs.
Experience with agentic AI architecture patterns, including single-agent and multi-agent workflows, supervisor/worker patterns, state and memory management, workflow orchestration, human approval gates, and safe action execution.
Proficiency with modern AI engineering frameworks and tools such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, Haystack, CrewAI, Hugging Face, or comparable open-source and cloud-native frameworks.
Strong programming skills in Python and modern software engineering practices, with familiarity in APIs, event-driven patterns, test automation, infrastructure as code, and scalable service design.
Proficiency in cloud AI/ML platforms and services such as Amazon Bedrock, AWS SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, Azure Machine Learning, Google Vertex AI, and related model hosting, retrieval, agent, and evaluation capabilities.
Experience with enterprise data and AI ecosystems such as Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Kafka, dbt, vector databases, lakehouse architectures, and modern data governance patterns.
Experience with MLOps, LLMOps, CI/CD, model and prompt versioning, automated evaluation, observability, containerization, Kubernetes, serverless deployment, and cost/performance optimization.
Strong understanding of AI architecture tradeoffs, including model selection, retrieval strategy, latency, accuracy, security, privacy, scalability, cost, vendor lock-in, and operating model implications.
Ability to communicate complex AI concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders, translating architecture choices into business value, delivery risk, and executive-level decisions.
Experience managing delivery teams and shaping AI/ML roadmaps, reference architectures, implementation backlogs, and adoption plans for enterprise clients.
Strong problem-solving, critical thinking, and business acumen, with the judgment to distinguish viable production solutions from prototype-only patterns.

About Us

Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries partner with clients to co-create powerful customer experiences, modern ways of working, and meaningful impact. 

What sets us apart? We believe work should be challenging and fulfilling, not perfect, but possible. That’s why we prioritize purpose, flexibility, connection, and recognition, so our people can thrive and love what they do, most days. 

Compensation and Benefits

Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, parental leave, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance.  

Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this role, we are hiring at the Principal level and targeted base pay salary range as follows: 

Boston, New Jersey, New York City, Washington DC, White Plains: $171,000 - $214,000
All other locations: $157,000 - $196,000

In addition, individuals may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.    

We are committed to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. If you have questions or concerns about the pay range or other compensation information in this posting, please contact us at: peopleone@slalom.com.

EEO and Accommodations

Slalom is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to attracting, developing and retaining highly qualified talent who empower our innovative teams through unique perspectives and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Slalom will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Slalom welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team or contact  accomodationrequest@slalom.com  if you require accommodations during the interview process.

jobs.title: Forward-Deployed Engineer / Solutions Architect - Onsite
jobs.description:
Job Title: Forward-Deployed Engineer / Solutions Architect - Onsite

Location: Irvine, CA - Onsite

### Role Summary

We are looking for a full-time Forward-Deployed Engineer / Solutions Architect to sit onsite with our client in Irvine, CA and lead delivery of an enterprise application on the Microsoft platform.

This person is the technical lead on the ground. They run discovery with business users, own the architecture, write code alongside the team, and direct an offshore pod of three developers and a QA analyst. They work daily with the client's platform architect and program manager.

This is a builder role, not a coordinator role. Program and project managers without recent hands-on development are not a fit.

### What You Will Build
The client has a working first version of the application and wants it extended through 2027.

Already in place:
A Dataverse data model, a PowerApps search app, document storage in SharePoint, and loaded historical records.

Planned phases:

Automated ingestion:
Monitor shared mailboxes and bring incoming items into the system, so users stop working in email
Better search,
plus roughly 20 UI improvements
Rollout to more business units
on the same codebase, with per-unit master data handled as configuration
AI drafting:
Generate draft responses from past approved answers, for human review

The PowerApp may be replaced by a custom React front end on the same data model.

### Key Responsibilities

Run discovery and requirements sessions directly with business users, and turn them into a solution design, backlog and estimates
Own the solution architecture across Dataverse, Power Platform, SharePoint and Azure, in agreement with the client's platform architect
Build hands-on: data model changes, automated email and document ingestion pipelines, search, and a React front end
Design and deliver AI features on Azure, including retrieval over historical records and drafted content for human review
Lead the offshore pod: break down work, review code, unblock developers, and own release quality
Hold the documentation and testing bar: requirements traceability, test plans, and QA sign-off before anything reaches business users
Report status, risks and timeline to client leadership, and flag scope changes early
Design for reuse, so the same codebase extends to additional business units through configuration

### Must-Have Qualifications

8+ years building enterprise software, including 3+ years as a solutions architect, technical lead or forward-deployed engineer
Production experience with Microsoft Power Platform: Dataverse data modeling and security, PowerApps, and Power Automate
Strong React with JavaScript or TypeScript, plus C#/.NET or Python for APIs and services
Azure experience: Functions or App Service, Microsoft Graph API for mail and SharePoint, Entra ID, and CI/CD
At least one LLM feature shipped to production on Azure OpenAI or Azure AI Foundry, such as retrieval-based search or document drafting
Has led a distributed team of three or more developers, including offshore
Runs workshops with non-technical users directly, and writes clear requirements and design documentation
Can be onsite in Irvine, CA, and is authorized to work in the United States

### Nice-to-Have Qualifications

Experience in life sciences, medical devices or another regulated industry, including validated systems or audit-ready documentation
Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility
Has replaced or extended a PowerApps solution with a custom React application on the same data model
Microsoft certifications such as Power Platform Solution Architect (PL-600) or Azure Solutions Architect (AZ-305)
Consulting or client services background

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer / Senior Algorithm Engineer
jobs.description:
About Xnurta Xnurta, powered by SparkX, is an AI-native retail media and advertising optimization platform for brands, sellers and agencies on Amazon and beyond. We combine multi-agent AI systems, predictive analytics and deep domain expertise to deliver advertising performance at scale.
About the Role Xnurta is strengthening its AI capabilities for advertising and commerce. We are looking for senior engineers who can independently own important technical problems and turn solutions into production systems.
This is a Senior Individual Contributor role; people management is not a requirement. Candidates may specialize in data, model training and optimization, or AI/agentic systems. We expect substantial depth in at least one area and effective collaboration across the others—not mastery of every part of the stack.
Specialization Tracks Data and Training Data: Data modeling, quality, lineage, feature and sample construction, and feedback-data management. Example: Turn business events, strategies, actions, and outcomes into trusted, reusable training and evaluation datasets; prevent leakage and training-serving inconsistencies
Model Training and Algorithm Optimization: Predictive/decision models or large language models; training, fine-tuning, evaluation, error analysis, and iteration. Example: Improve task effectiveness, budget allocation, or execution quality; design sound offline evaluations and online controlled experiments
AI / Agentic Systems: Tool use, workflow orchestration, state management, permissions, execution reliability, and observability. Example: Build agents that complete real tasks, including retries, idempotency, approvals, failure recovery, and outcome feedback

Responsibilities Own a critical component end to end. Take responsibility from problem definition and technical design through implementation, testing, and production release.
Solve core problems within your specialization. Improve data quality, train and optimize models, or build reliable AI/agentic systems, working with upstream and downstream teams to complete integration.
Validate improvements through experiments. Establish reproducible evaluations and appropriate baselines. Separate model, data, and engineering issues; connect offline results to real-world value.
Own production quality. Monitor reliability, effectiveness, latency, and cost per task. Improve observability, diagnosis, and rollback mechanisms.
Build reusable capabilities. Contribute code, data standards, evaluation tools, and documentation that support multiple product lines, collaborating with teams in the U.S. and China.

Required Qualifications Deep expertise and demonstrated results in at least one specialization above, with the ability to explain the problem, approach, personal contribution, and validation method.
Experience deploying systems into production or delivering technology used by real users, with the ability to resolve data, engineering, and effectiveness issues beyond the prototype stage.
Strong coding skills. Model/data specialists should be proficient in Python and relevant tools; systems specialists should bring strong backend or distributed-systems engineering skills. No single framework is prescribed.
Sound understanding of data quality, experiment design, and evaluation, including whether an improvement is reproducible, meaningful to the business, and worth its operating cost.
Clear English technical communication and documentation skills, and the ability to collaborate across Product, ML, Data, Engineering, and geographic locations.

Preferred Qualifications Practical experience in model training/fine-tuning, inference optimization, agent evaluation, tool execution, or learning from outcome feedback.
Experience in advertising, recommendations, search, forecasting, budget optimization, commerce, or enterprise automation. Advertising experience is not a universal prerequisite for this role.
Startup or zero-to-one experience, with an interest in understanding user problems directly, testing quickly, and iterating based on evidence.
Strong open-source, research, or technical work connected to real engineering problems. Publications, degrees, and employer prestige do not substitute for delivery ability.

Initial Priorities Understand the assigned component's data, system interfaces, current effectiveness, and main bottlenecks.
Deliver a verifiable technical improvement with a clear comparison against the relevant baseline.
Integrate the improvement into production, with monitoring, documentation, and reusable engineering support.

Location & Compensation Location: Campbell, CA (hybrid), full-time
Base salary range: $100,000–$300,000 per year. Final pay depends on level, experience, skills and location. Benefits include medical, dental and vision.

Xnurta is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic.

jobs.description:
In most instances, this position requires in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
5 years of experience programming in Python or C++.
3 years of experience testing, maintaining, or launching software products, and 1 year of experience with software design and architecture.
3 years of experience with end-to-end Machine Learning (e.g., model deployment, model evaluation, data processing, debugging).
1 year of experience with state of the art GenAI techniques (e.g., LLMs, Multi-Modal, Large Vision Models) or with GenAI-related concepts (language modeling, computer vision).

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or related technical field.
5 years of experience with data structures/algorithms.
1 year of experience in a technical leadership role.
Experience developing accessible technologies.

About The Job

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Join Google Search AI and work at the intersection of industry leading

global scale. We apply breakthrough research, leveraging models like Gemini, to launch high-impact products that help billions ask any question and get things done. If you want to drive the future of AI in Search and work with world-class experts to deliver tangible, global impact and continuous innovation, this is the place.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Bioengineering
jobs.description:
Merge Labs is a frontier research lab with the mission of bridging biological and artificial intelligence to maximize human ability, agency and experience. We’re pursuing this goal by developing fundamentally new approaches to brain-computer interfaces that interact with the brain at high bandwidth, integrate with advanced AI, and are ultimately safe and accessible for anyone to use.

About The Team

Merge is building the next generation of brain-computer interfaces by combining recent advances in synthetic biology, neuroscience, AI, and non-invasive imaging. To support this mission, we are building a cross-functional data-science group which sits at the intersection of computational modeling, neuroscience, and biomolecular engineering. This group collaborates extensively with wet-lab scientists, automation engineers, and data engineers to create ML frameworks that accelerate molecule discovery and device optimization.

About The Role

We need a Data-Scientist who can sit at the interface of Ultrasound, synthetic-biology, and research platforms (imaging, sequencing) and drive the development of rigorous data-analysis pipelines that surface actionable insights for experimental and computational researchers alike. This person will collaborate with domain experts in ML, Ultrasound, synthetic biology, and data-engineering to develop data-analysis pipelines that transform “raw” data into actionable artifacts. This person will subsequently collaborate with ML researchers to develop and run ML pipelines that enable de-novo design and closed-loop active learning cycles across a number of problem domains in bioengineering (delivery, immunology, synthetic biology, protein-engineering).

In this role, you will:

Collaborate with wet-lab scientists to define tractable optimization objectives and metrics, and encode domain specific priors and constraints for downstream computational modeling.
Stay current with research in Synthetic Biology and ML-guided molecular and cellular engineering, as well as data-analysis methods and techniques for biological data (OMICS, Agentic-workflows).
Contribute to the long-term research roadmap and serve as a thought-leader for scientists.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

Deep grounding in synthetic biology, molecular engineering, and computational methods for data-analysis.
Experience in biomolecular ultrasound.
Familiarity with fundamental concepts in NGS, Omics, ML, and molecular engineering.
Proficiency in Python / PyTorch / BoTorch / Pyro and comfort writing clean, reproducible production grade code.
Experience bridging machine learning and experimental science, especially working with sparse, noisy, and or high-cost data.

If you're excited about this role but don't meet every qualification, please apply. As we build, we're hiring for complementary strengths to form a high-impact team.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist Field Engineer - AI Training and HPC
jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

What You’ll Do

The Customer Experience (CX) Organization
at CoreWeave is dedicated to ensuring every client running AI workloads at scale has a seamless, reliable, and high-performance experience. This team supports the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution—working across data centers, hardware systems, and customer workloads to maintain the integrity of our cloud platform. The CX organization aligns closely with the internal and customer engineering teams, offering valuable insights from the field and having the chance to contribute to the CoreWeave product roadmap and development.

About The Role

CoreWeave runs some of the largest GPU clusters in the world for the AI labs and enterprises that train models on them. As a Senior Specialist Field Engineer
for AI Training and HPC
, you'll help customers get the most out of those clusters across the whole training lifecycle: pre-training runs on thousands of GPUs, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, evaluation, and the HPC workloads that share the same schedulers and fabrics. You'll work closely with the HPC and AI platform product and engineering teams, and what you learn in the field will help shape what they build.

In This Role, You Will

Lead technical discovery with customers: understand their models, training pipelines, and scale, and turn that into a design they can run on CoreWeave.
Agree on POC success criteria with the customer, run the POC, and turn its results into a production deployment plan.
Design how customers run training on CoreWeave: Slurm and Kubernetes scheduling, partition and QoS policy, topology-aware placement, and shared storage for datasets and checkpoints.
Design fine-tuning and RL pipelines: SFT and RL jobs, rollout generation, reward and verifier execution, evaluation gates for model promotion, and the handoff to serving.
Troubleshoot problems that span the scheduler, the container runtime, NCCL, NVLink, the InfiniBand or RoCE fabric, the GPU driver stack, and storage, across jobs that run on thousands of GPUs for weeks.
Adapt and migrate customer training, fine-tuning, and evaluation pipelines to CoreWeave. Integrate and troubleshoot their frameworks, data loading, checkpoint and resume paths, experiment tracking, and job observability. Build reusable integrations and reference implementations from recurring patterns.
Design and tune GPU-accelerated HPC workloads on the same platform: MPI applications, simulation, and scientific computing codes.
Find where the product falls short for real training workloads and help the engineering teams fill those gaps.
Lead customer technical overviews and workshops, with occasional travel.

Who You Are

B.S. in Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
7+ years building, operating, or supporting large-scale distributed systems, ML training infrastructure, or HPC environments, as a systems, platform, ML, or research engineer, or in a deeply technical field role.
Have run, supported, or troubleshot large multi-node GPU jobs in production on Slurm or Kubernetes, for training or HPC, and understand scheduling policy, preemption, and how jobs fail at scale.
Hands-on with the stack under a distributed job: NCCL or MPI, the NVIDIA driver and CUDA stack, RDMA over InfiniBand or RoCE, and the tools for finding a bad link, a bad GPU, or a bad kernel version in a thousand-node job.
Deep in at least one of the following, with working knowledge of the other two:
Have led technical work directly with customers or internal platform users: gathered requirements, set success criteria, and delivered against them.
Comfortable reading and writing code: reading source, from a Slurm plugin to a PyTorch distributed backend to an RL framework, to answer a question rather than waiting for the owning team, and writing the tools, reproductions, and reference implementations customers need.
Able to explain technical problems clearly to engineers and executives, building trust with customers.

Preferred

Rack-scale systems such as GB200 and GB300 NVL72: IMEX, multi-rack NVLink domains, and the scheduling and failure modes they introduce.
Slurm internals: have written or modified plugins, prolog and epilog logic, or accounting integrations.
Contributions to Slurm, NCCL, Kueue, TRL, verl, OpenRLHF, or similar open-source scheduling or training projects.
Kueue, Topology-Aware Scheduling, Volcano, or Run:ai on Kubernetes.
Experience with experiment tracking and model registry systems at team scale, and with the governance around them (lineage, approval, rollback, audit).
Capacity planning for large multi-tenant deployments.
Published work or conference talks (SC, MLSys, HPDC, NSDI) on large-scale training systems, RL infrastructure, or LLM evaluation.

Wondering if you’re a good fit?
We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match.
Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.

You'd rather read the NCCL trace than guess why the step time doubled.
You're comfortable saying "I don't know yet," and then you go find out.
You like working on a hard problem alongside the customer and the engineering team, and you share the credit.

Why CoreWeave?

About

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

Be Curious at Your Core
Act Like an Owner
Empower Employees
Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for take off, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

An AI agent is only as useful as what it knows about your company. For many of the world's leading companies, that knowledge lives in Notion. The AI Knowledge & Capabilities team makes sure every agent working in Notion – built by Notion, by customers, or by other AI companies – finds the right answer, quickly and at a cost that makes sense.

We own the systems that make this work: search, knowledge, and memory. We also own the agent harness – the tools, context, and model choices that turn a model into a working agent. We decide what to build using evals, customer feedback, and product judgment. Our work reaches users directly, and other AI teams at Notion build on it.

We recently shipped Memories, so Notion AI, Custom Agents, and agents connected through MCP can learn and remember across platforms. We also shipped Auto, a model router that delivers frontier quality at 90% lower cost. Next, we're bringing memory, search, and the harness together into one system. Nobody has figured out how to package that yet – we want any company to get a great knowledge system for its agents with a click or a few questions.

You will be a technical leader for the team. You'll set direction across search, knowledge, and the harness, starting hands-on with making agents better and cheaper, and help define how Notion measures AI quality.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve

Set technical direction for search, knowledge, and the agent harness – make the architecture calls, run design reviews, and decide what the team builds next.
Make Notion's agents better, faster, and cheaper – starting with the harness: which tools an agent can call, what context it gets, and which model handles each request.
Lead how we measure agent quality – evolve the metrics and evals that reflect real usage, and use them to choose what ships.
Turn company data into answers agents can use – build agentic search and memory that give every agent the context it needs, at the right latency and cost.
Work closely with research – partner with Notion's model research team on evals, model choice, and models trained for agentic work, and get what works into production. You'll also work with search platform and AI product teams on work that spans teams.
Grow the team – mentor engineers, review designs, and develop the next tech leads.

Skills You'll Need To Bring

Production applied AI: You've shipped and iterated on production LLM or agent systems used by real users. You owned how their quality was measured, and you changed course based on what you found.
Quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs: You've traded quality against latency and cost in a production system, measured the result, and can explain what you gave up and why.
Technical leadership: You've owned the technical direction of a complex system, often across teams, and kept it sound as it grew. You don't wait for a roadmap – you find the problems worth solving, make the case for them, and go deep on the hardest ones yourself.
Product sense: You've shipped quality improvements users noticed, and you've shaped new products from scratch – from the data model to what users see. You can explain why they mattered.
Shipping something new: You've taken an idea from nothing to a product people use. You try new models and tools early, form your own views, and turn them into product decisions.
Making other engineers better: You mentor engineers at every level, guide their designs, and share what you know so it scales past you. Multiple engineers have grown by working with you.
Clear communication: You write clearly about tradeoffs, disagree directly, and change your mind when the evidence says to.

Nice To Haves

You've improved LLM cost and quality directly – e.g. model routing, eval-driven harness or prompt tuning, or token efficiency in long-running agents.
You've founded a company or been an early engineer at a startup, and built systems that hold up at large scale.
Experience working closely with research or model training teams.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About The Role

Bedrock Robotics is hiring a Data Scientist to lead the work on Simulation: measuring how realistic our simulator is, and when its results can be trusted. In this role, you will operate as a senior technical individual contributor, partnering closely with simulation, autonomy, machine learning, and evaluation teams to compare simulated runs with real-world data generated by autonomous construction machines and their operators.

You will own the statistical methods behind simulation-based testing (realism metrics, calibration against field data, and the design of simulation experiments) while helping establish foundational practices for how data science is applied at Bedrock. This role is ideal for a senior-to-staff-level data scientist with a strong statistics foundation and experience with simulation or physical systems, who enjoys working close to the engineers building the simulator.

What You'll Do

Own data science for simulation, focusing on the gaps between simulation and the field that most affect release decisions
Analyze field logs and simulated runs side by side to find where simulated machine, soil, and truck behavior departs from reality
Define and track realism metrics that compare distributions of simulated and real behavior (cycle times, bucket fill, arm trajectories, soil response, truck interactions) across simulator versions
Design simulation experiments (number of runs, scenario mix, variance reduction, sequential tests) so comparisons between software versions are powered and unbiased
Collaborate closely with simulation and data engineering teams to extract scenarios from field logs and keep simulated and real data comparable
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, influencing roadmap and design decisions
Contribute to the foundation of data science practices at Bedrock, helping shape how future work and teams scale
Validate simulation as a predictor: measure how well simulation results predict field outcomes of software releases, and set when a simulation result is strong enough to act on
Calibrate simulator parameters (for example terrain material properties) against field data, with uncertainty
Find which parts of the simulator (soil physics, hydraulics, sensors, other agents) drive the gap to reality, and help simulation engineers prioritize fixes
Build scenario sampling so simulated test suites represent field conditions, and use importance sampling to estimate rare-event rates

What We're Looking For

Required

Experience validating a simulator or physical model against real-world data
5+ years of experience in data science, applied statistics, or applied machine learning, including work on simulation or physical systems
Comfort operating as a senior IC in a fast-growing startup, balancing execution with technical judgment and prioritization
Ability to work independently, define analytical approaches, and drive projects from concept to insight
Experience working with complex, high-volume time-series data from robots, vehicles, or other physical systems
Strong grounding in statistics: experimental design, variance estimation, comparing distributions, and calibrating models to data, with a track record of influencing decisions through data
Hands-on experience collaborating with simulation, data engineering, and infrastructure teams on data pipelines, data quality, and scalable analysis workflows
Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using modern tooling like agentic AI
Master’s degree in Statistics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred

Experience with simulation for autonomous vehicles or robotics (realism metrics, simulated agents, scenario-based testing)
Experience with physics simulation, multibody dynamics, or granular materials
Experience with rare-event estimation, importance sampling, or surrogate models (e.g., Gaussian processes)
Experience with learned or generative world models
PhD in a quantitative field

jobs.description:
Description

If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/

About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

About The Role

We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision.

Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office.

You Will

Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other.
Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data.
Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months.
Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap.
Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality.
Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists.

Perks

Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance
401(k)
Maternity & Parental Leave
Flexible PTO
Amazon Employee Discount

About The Team

Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of data scientist experience
A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience.
3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails.
Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results.
Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R.
A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

An MS or PhD in a quantitative field.
Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems.
Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals.
Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling).
Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply.
Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces.
Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!).

About Us

Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

Why We Exist

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.
No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.

First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"
Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.
Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

4+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.
Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.
Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.
Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

jobs.description:
At Eve, we’re redefining what’s possible in legal technology. Our mission is to empower plaintiff law firms with AI that helps them handle more cases, recover more for clients, and grow.

We believe the future of law will be built by AI-Native Law Firms — firms managed, scaled, and optimized by intelligent systems, rather than manual processes and endless administrative work. Eve augments attorneys across every stage of a case — from intake to document review to strategy and settlement — so they can focus on what truly matters: achieving the best outcomes for their clients.

Our vision: enable every plaintiff firm to operate at its highest potential, powered by AI purpose-built for the way they work.

Why Join Eve

Product-market fit:
Eve is used by over 1800+ law firms, and we’re growing fast.

Backed by top investors:
We’ve raised over $160M from world-class partners including Spark Capital, Andreessen Horowitz(A16z), Menlo Ventures, and Lightspeed.

Built by a world-class team:
Engineers, designers, and operators from places like Scale, Meta, Airbnb, Cruise, Square, Rubrik, and Lyft are building Eve from the ground up.

AI-Native from day one:
We’re on the bleeding edge of AI, collaborating directly with teams at OpenAI and Anthropic to build best-in-class AI workflows tailored for legal work.

Explosive growth:
We are rowing 4X year over year.

About This Opportunity

Every plaintiff firm's next case starts with a phone call. At Eve, more and more of those calls are answered by our AI voice agent, which qualifies potential clients and creates leads with no human in the loop. It is the only part of Eve that talks directly to a firm's future clients. When it's set up well, firms catch every lead. When it isn't, callers hang up and sign somewhere else. As an Intake AI Architect, you're the person who gets firms there. You own intake setup end to end, and the voice agent becomes your deepest specialty: barge-in and turn-taking, staying on script across long multi-branch flows, tool calls that don't leave the caller in dead air, and callers who go off script entirely. Today that knowledge lives in a few people's heads. We are hiring the person who owns it. You won't do it alone: you'll work hand in hand with Eve's dedicated Intake product and engineering team and can lean on them heavily. This is both a build role and a product one. You'll see every intake setup at Eve, which makes you the strongest voice on what's hard and what the platform should do next. It's a new role. You'll define as much as you execute, and shape how it grows.

Location and travel:
On-site in San Francisco or San Mateo preferred, open to remote. Expect regular travel to client sites. If you're remote, plan on about one week a month in the Bay Area with the Intake team.

What You'll Do

Own intake setup end to end. Map how leads actually reach the firm, then take it to "onboarding complete": the voice agent, phone system, lead sources, lead management and document systems, and scoring. The Customer Success Manager owns the account. You own whether the firm's intake works. Success is firms live and staying live, not configs shipped. No more firms disappearing mid-setup.
Make the voice agent fit. Translate what the firm asks for into what it actually needs, configure the agent, take it live, and iterate on real calls until the firm is happy.
Shape the product. Bring what you see across every firm back to product and engineering. You'll be the strongest voice on what gets built next for intake.
Make firm requests disappear. Handle change requests fast, then fix the root cause in the product or the default templates so the next firm never has to ask.
Help build how Eve evals voice agents. Turn the test calls and call reviews you'd run anyway into a repeatable process. With product and engineering, define what "the voice agent did the right thing" means for our hardest firms, and test it against model and platform upgrades, interruptions, off-script callers, and long flows.
Be the expert others learn from. Write the runbooks and training that let Customer Success and our Legal AI Architects, who build custom AI agents for firms, run 80% of intake setups without you, so your time goes to the hardest firms and the product.

Problems You'll Take On

A firm going live next week with a complicated transfer tree: take it from questionnaire to live calls and tune it until every transfer lands.
A voice agent that fumbles existing clients calling for case updates: rework the call flow and prove it on real calls.
Leads from a firm's referral partners that never reach Eve: trace the gap and close it.
The call reviews you'd run anyway: turn them into a repeatable test set that catches problems before the firm does.

What You'll Work With

Eve's voice agent platform: the prompts, configuration, and admin tooling that power every firm's voice agent
Call recordings, transcripts, and lead data for every firm you support
Eval tooling, including an internal Slack agent that builds and runs eval datasets, plus Braintrust
Each firm's own stack: phone systems, web forms and chat, lead management systems like Lead Docket, document management

What We Are Looking For

3+ years of experience in intake, legal operations, implementation, or building with AI.
You know intake from the inside. You've run or worked intake at a plaintiff firm or a similar high-volume, phone-first operation, or you've implemented intake systems for firms. You know the edge cases: the catastrophic-injury caller who needs a partner now, the existing client calling the intake line for a case update, the caller whose statute of limitations runs out next week, the conflict check before anyone promises anything.
You test AI, or want to. You've written evals, test-call scripts, or regression checklists for an AI system, or you're eager to learn how. You'd rather prove the voice agent works than assume it does.
You hear the real ask, then build it. An intake manager says "make the voice agent friendlier" and you figure out what they mean, explain the plan clearly, then configure it yourself.
You're fearless with systems. Phone trees, call forwarding, CRMs, webhooks, admin portals. You're the one who gets on a screen share with a firm's phone vendor and figures it out, then writes it down so the next firm never needs the call

Nice to Haves

Comfort with code. If you can contribute back to in-product tooling, build your own tools, or improve the voice agent platform itself, that's incredible
Experience with voice AI platforms (Retell, Vapi, LiveKit, Twilio) or contact center tooling
Hands-on experience with legal tech like Lead Docket, Litify, Filevine, or Clio
Prior forward deployed, solutions engineering, or implementation work

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASELAYER

Every business in America needs a bank account to exist. The system that decides whether they're real, who's behind them, and whether they're a risk, runs on infrastructure from the 1980s. We're rebuilding that layer from scratch.
Baselayer is the identity layer for institutions across the United States — the most complete business graph in America and every human tied to it. We fuse public records, IRS data, sanctions lists, web signals, and fraud telemetry from 2,200+ financial institutions into a single graph that resolves any business and the humans behind it in milliseconds. The legacy credit bureaus took 50 years to build something that gets 60% match rates. We've built something that gets 98% in under two years.
Today we're trusted by over 20% of financial institutions in America — including FIS, Rho, Socure and leading loan infrastructure providers. But the graph is becoming infrastructure for anyone who needs to know if a business is real and worth trusting: gig platforms, marketplaces, AI companies, and commerce infrastructure at scale.
Trust is the substrate of every financial transaction. We're rebuilding it.
ABOUT THE TEAM

AI agents are starting to transact: opening accounts, buying services, moving money on behalf of the businesses and people behind them. Every one of those transactions has a counterparty asking the question banks have always asked: who am I dealing with, and can I trust them? Today's identity infrastructure wasn't built to answer it at agent speed.
The Agentic Economy team is extending Baselayer's business graph into the trust layer for agentic commerce: verifiable credentials that bind an agent to the verified business and human behind it, a registry counterparties can query in real time, and verification APIs that plug into the networks, platforms, and protocols where agent transactions happen.
We run like a startup inside a startup: a small senior team led by our GM of Agentic Economy, working directly with payment networks, banks, wallet providers, and agent platforms. The category is being defined right now; the standards, seats, and infrastructure decisions of the next 18 months will be consequential for a decade.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You're the engineering arm of the Agentic Economy team: the person who turns partner conversations into working software. You'll ship the surfaces partners and their agents actually touch: verification APIs, our MCP server, credential flows, demos, and reference implementations. When a payment network wants to see real-time counterparty verification inside an agentic checkout, you build it, often within days.
You'll sit in technical calls with partners, scope integrations on the spot, and work closely with our core platform engineering while owning the last mile yourself. This is a role for an engineer who wants the field, not just the repo.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Ship partner integrations of our agentic economy products from first technical call to production
Build prototypes, demos, and reference implementations for partner meetings, communities, and conferences, often on short notice
Own the developer- and agent-facing quality of our surfaces: API ergonomics, documentation, sample repos, sandbox environments, integration guides, technical posts
Get our MCP server listed, featured, and performing in the connection hubs, directories, and marketplaces where agent builders look
Optimize the agent-facing experience itself: tool descriptions, response design, error handling 
Show up in agent builder communities (Discord servers, hackathons, working groups, open-source repos) as a builder
Be the engineering voice in partner calls; translate partner constraints into clear specs for the core platform team
Feed field learnings back into the product roadmap alongside our PM and GM

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS 5+ years shipping production software; strong TypeScript and/or Python
Deep API design and integration experience: REST, webhooks, OAuth/JWT auth flows
You've worked directly with customers or partners
Hands-on with the modern agent stack: MCP, LLM tool-calling, agent frameworks
Can take a demo from idea to working in days, and an integration to production in weeks
Thrive in ambiguity: startup pace, end-to-end ownership

At Commure, our Air AI team is building the intelligence layer that lives inside the clinical workflow, that listens, documents, reasons, and acts so clinicians don't have to. You'll work across documentation that transcribes patient visits and structures them into clinical notes in real-time, a conversational clinical assistant grounded in live patient context and medical literature, and an extensible AI Skills Library of reusable agents and workflows that automates clinical tasks across the platform. If you want to build AI that clinicians trust with their most critical work, this is that team.

What You'll Do

Leverage and build on top of AI/LLM technologies to accelerate product development and deliver intelligent, automated experiences to clinicians and patients
Design and influence decisions that shape our fullstack architecture for scalable, AI-powered healthcare solutions
Lead or contribute to technical planning for new features, balancing feasibility, clinical usability, and business impact
Establish best practices for code quality, testing, deployment, and observability
Mentor engineers across the team, raising the bar on design patterns, code standards, and technical thinking
Collaborate with product managers, designers, and clinical experts to ship intuitive solutions that work in real clinical environments
Be part of a fast-moving team that celebrates large ambition, ships daily, and makes decisions quickly

What You Have

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, required
Professional software engineering experience, ideally in a high-growth or startup environment
Strong fullstack skills — Python on the backend (required), TypeScript/React on the frontend, with working knowledge of containers and cloud (Docker, Kubernetes)
Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs or building AI-powered features in production

Strong debugging and problem-solving skills with a history of demonstrated resourcefulness
Strong communication skills — comfortable working with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders including clinical teams
Experience in fast-moving environments where shipping quickly is the norm

What You'll Do

Utilize the latest developments in LLM technology to automate the reverse-engineering of electronic health records.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (product, engineering, and healthcare) to gather integration requirements, define technical approaches, and prioritize tasks based on business needs.
Contribute to the technical direction of the integration platform by proposing and implementing improvements to architecture, tools, and technologies.
Take ownership of end-to-end integration workflows, from design and development through to deployment and post-launch monitoring.
Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, troubleshoot integration issues, and proactively improve the reliability of integrations in production environments.
Ensure all integration work adheres to healthcare compliance and security standards (e.g., HIPAA, HL7, FHIR) and collaborate with security teams to protect sensitive data.
Work closely with junior engineers to provide technical guidance and mentorship, helping them solve problems and ensuring high-quality code standards are followed.
Drive the implementation of best practices for integration development, including testing, error handling, version control, and continuous integration.
Collaborate with DevOps and QA teams to implement monitoring and alerting systems that ensure integration reliability and system health in production.
Stay up-to-date with industry trends in healthcare technology, integration patterns, and emerging tools, continuously suggesting and applying innovations that can improve system performance and integration capabilities.
Participate in agile development cycles, contributing to sprint planning, retrospectives, and maintaining a collaborative and efficient working environment

5+ years of professional software development industry experience
Proficiency in backend languages like Python, Go, or C++.
Proficiency in frontend languages like Javascript, HTML, CSS
Experience including but not limited to Git, GCP / AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, relational and non-relational DBs, and monitoring/alerting tools
Proven track record of designing and implementing end-to-end solutions and making successful architectural decisions
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Merge is tackling some of the most audacious problems in molecular engineering, synthetic biology and neuroscience. Our Research Platform Team builds the experimental capabilities needed to solve these problems with very high speed and rigor. The instruments and pipelines the team builds accelerate molecular assembly, protein expression, mammalian cell culture, advanced microscopy, sequencing, as well as some very unusual custom methods. The team collaborates with program teams to establish and streamline these capabilities, automate wherever it makes sense to do so, and integrate with our data science and machine learning pipelines. We come up with creative approaches to greatly increase throughput and continuously innovate.

As an Automation Engineer, you will build automation pipelines to enable key research programs to move as quickly as possible. The role will leverage your existing technical and scientific expertise while requiring you to rapidly learn new scientific domains and develop new experimental capabilities. You will collaborate closely with program leads, project scientists, data scientists and engineers to co-design, implement and scale research pipelines. Partner with program, assay development, software and ML colleagues to develop plans for automated research instrumentation.

Collaborate with data science/ML engineers to integrate metadata tracking, computational design, and analysis into experimental pipelines.

Have a background in engineering, robotics or similar field with experience in a biological context.

Love getting your hands dirty with equipment setup, code writing and data analysis — whatever is needed.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Finance
jobs.description:
About Us

At Rox, we believe in empowering people to do their best work.

Our platform supercharges sellers with autonomous revenue agents to do the manual work so they can focus on what they do best: selling. Just as coding agents 10x’d engineering, revenue agents 10x customer work.

We are reimagining the revenue stack by building the world’s first revenue operating system, from the application layer to the system of context. With Rox, humans are evolving to orchestrators while agents manage the end-to-end customer lifecycle.

Rox powers Global 2000 leaders in banking, hardware, construction, and sovereign AI, while serving dominant AI winners like Ramp and Cognition.

Underlying all of this success is a unwavering, shared belief in the mission, with an unreasonable commitment of doing whatever it takes to make it a reality.

The Team

Nothing is possible without the world-class team, assembled to redefine how businesses operate.

Members On Our Team Have

Founded and exited successful companies
Held the highest positions at Google, AWS, Confluent, and New Relic
Won IMO and IOI gold medals
Published field-defining papers

We’re backed by the best, having raised $50M from Sequoia (Alfred Lin), General Catalyst (Hemant Taneja), Google Ventures, Elad Gil, and Chris Ré.

Core Principles

Taste:
Craft beautiful experiences.

No matter how small, we strive to make sure every detail is right. We care deeply about every interaction, both in terms of whether it helps the seller get the job done, but also how the product makes them feel. We get a visceral feeling when something is off and stop at nothing to make sure we make it right. We never settle, continuously exploring ways to delight sellers.

Obsession:
Commit unreasonably.

In all aspects of our craft, we commit. We not only are immediately reactive to customers’ requests but are proactive about driving value even before they ask. We are also obsessive about always learning and honing our craft, improving ourselves and product every single day.

Action:
Get it done.

Talking is easy but the difference comes from the execution. We lean heavily towards making thoughtful yet fast decisions and delivering immediately. We play in a field where trust is paramount. We earn the trust and right to empower the best sellers by forging a history of over-delivering on the promise at record speed.

Role

As a Finance Data Scientist at Rox, you will own the numbers that explain what it costs to run an agentic product and what we earn from it. Every agent action has a real cost in models, enrichment and infrastructure. Your work tells the company which products and customers are profitable, why, and what to change.

You will sit between Finance, Engineering and GTM. You will build the cost and margin models, reconcile contracts and revenue across systems, catch cost anomalies before they reach the P&L, and give leadership a view of unit economics they can run the business on.

This is a high-ownership role on a small data team. You will be as comfortable in a dbt model as in a month-end close conversation, and you will be expected to push back with evidence when a number does not tie.

You'll be one of Rox's first dedicated data hires. It's an opportunity to help build an agile data function from the ground up at an early-stage, fast-growing company.

Responsibilities

Own COGS reporting end to end: LLM, enrichment vendor and infrastructure costs.
Build and maintain gross margin reporting by product and customer, tied out to the general ledger and delivered to Finance and leadership on a set cadence.
Track cost per action and its drivers, and partner with Engineering to triage the most expensive workloads and push margins higher.
Run cost anomaly detection so that a model change, a vendor price change or a runaway workflow is flagged in days, not at month end.
Build the single source of truth for contracts, ARR and revenue across the CRM, the ERP and the warehouse, including the closed-won to ARR process.
Model consumption against contract commitments to support pricing, packaging, overage and renewal decisions.
Produce the repeatable business metrics pack for the board and investors: ARR, net retention, gross margin and unit economics, with definitions that hold up to diligence.
Build and maintain the dbt models and Snowflake pipelines behind all of the above, including vendor billing and ERP data ingestion.

Qualifications

Required

Degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Finance)
2 to 5+ years in analytics, FP&A, strategic finance or data science at a fast-growing company, with direct ownership of cost, margin or revenue models
Strong SQL and Python, comfortable with large, messy billing, metering and usage data
Working knowledge of SaaS finance: ARR, revenue recognition basics, COGS versus opex, gross margin and net retention
Experience with dbt and a modern warehouse, and with dashboards in Sigma, Looker, Tableau, Mode or equivalent
A reconciliation habit: you tie numbers to source systems and can explain every variance
Able to explain a cost or margin finding to both an engineer and a CFO
High energy, "no job is too small" mentality, and extreme ownership
Located in or willing to relocate to San Francisco

Preferred

Experience at a consumption or usage-based business (e.g., Datadog, New Relic, Snowflake), with fluency in usage metering and unit economics
Experience with the cost structure of AI products: token pricing, model routing and third-party data vendors
Experience with ERP and billing systems, and with getting their data into a warehouse
Experience supporting a fundraise, audit or board reporting cycle
Experience with pricing and packaging analysis
Comfort with AI-native development tools such as Cursor and Claude Code

Benefits

Competitive pay with considerable equity upside
Health Insurance
