The Senior AI Engineer I
is a hands-on engineer accountable for end-to-end AI capabilities within a product or across multiple products, from design and build through operation in production. Scope includes retrieval and context assembly, model and agentic logic, integration with source systems and consuming applications, monitoring and evaluation, and operational runbook maintenance. Depth is expected in two or three of these capability areas, with working familiarity across the rest.

The role also covers the engineering that makes these capabilities trustworthy in business use. This includes evaluation and regression testing, human-in-the-loop and other AI-specific security controls, and accountability for inference cost and latency.

The role builds on the shared platform services and reference implementations set by the Principal AI Engineer, within the target-state architecture set by the Data/AI Platform Architect. It also takes handover of capabilities built by technical delivery partners and maintains them in production.

Role Responsibilities:

Design, build, operate, and own end-to-end AI capabilities within a product or across multiple products, spanning retrieval and context assembly; model and agentic logic; integration with source systems and consuming applications (APIs, MCPs, authentication); monitoring and evaluation; and operational runbook maintenance
Train and evaluate machine learning models for well-scoped problems such as classification, regression, anomaly detection, clustering, and forecasting, using operational and commercial data. Determine when and how to use ML models versus simpler statistical baselines
Build retrieval and context pipelines against enterprise content using chunking, tagging, and a metadata strategy. Measure and report retrieval quality against a defined standard
Design and maintain evaluation for these capabilities, including offline evals, automated scoring such as LLM-as-judge, and regression tests that run on every prompt or pipeline change to ensure quality before release. Monitor quality and drift signals in production
Own inference cost and latency in production, tracking cost per transaction and end-to-end response time, and profiling where that time is spent. Make tradeoffs where needed to stay within agreed targets
Implement human-in-the-loop and AI-specific security controls, including shadow and assisted modes, confidence and citation surfaces, override capture, audit trails, identity-scoped retrieval, input and output guardrails, tool permissions, and prompt injection resistance
Take handover of application components built by technical delivery partners: read the code, close operational gaps, update the runbook, and maintain them in production
Improve team efficiency by establishing reusable components and reference examples, reviewing code, and onboarding new engineers

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, another STEM field, or a related discipline required

Practical experience developing ML models for supervised and unsupervised problems
Experience building and maintaining evaluation and regression testing for AI and ML systems
Working knowledge of AI-specific security and responsible AI controls
Competent use of coding agents and other AI-assisted tooling, including scoping the right tasks for them, reviewing generated code, and recognizing which tasks are a poor fit for delegation
Experience with IT/OT environments, industrial data sources, or operational technology systems is preferred

new_jobs.description:
Senior Data & AI / LLM Engineer

Build practical AI for complex, real-world challenges

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior Data & AI / LLM Engineer to create and operate modern data, machine learning, and generative AI solutions in a complex, regulated industry.

You’ll work across the full engineering lifecycle: understanding business needs, exploring data, designing solutions, building pipelines and AI applications, and deploying reliable production code in Azure. You’ll partner with business and technical teams to turn ambiguous challenges into secure, useful tools.

We value engineers who use AI thoughtfully in their own work. You’ll have opportunities to use tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude to speed up development, testing, documentation, and maintenance, while applying sound judgment to the code they produce.

What you’ll do

Build trusted data products

Design, build, test, and maintain data pipelines and products using Databricks, Spark/PySpark, Delta Lake, SQL, and Python.
Explore complex datasets to find patterns, anomalies, trends, and opportunities.
Develop ingestion, transformation, integration, and data-quality processes for structured and unstructured data.
Work with data from cloud platforms, APIs, files, databases, and enterprise applications.
Improve data quality, lineage, observability, metadata, security, and governance.
Tune pipelines and workloads for reliability, performance, scale, and cost.

Put analytics and machine learning to work

Develop, evaluate, deploy, and monitor machine learning models using Python and appropriate frameworks.
Apply techniques such as classification, regression, clustering, feature engineering, and model evaluation.
Choose the right approach for each problem, whether analytics, traditional machine learning, or generative AI.
Partner with data scientists, subject matter experts, and engineering teams to bring analytical solutions into production.

Create useful LLM applications

Design and build LLM applications for tasks such as document processing, summarization, information extraction, classification, conversational assistance, and agentic workflows.
Apply patterns such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, embeddings, vector search, chunking, grounding, tool calling, and structured outputs.
Evaluate solutions for accuracy, relevance, hallucination risk, latency, cost, security, and responsible AI.
Connect structured data and unstructured content in secure, governed applications.
Build reusable AI components and APIs for broader enterprise use.

Deliver production-ready software in Azure

Build and deploy solutions across Azure services, including Azure Databricks, Storage and Data Lake, Microsoft Entra ID, Key Vault, Azure Functions, APIs, and Azure AI services.
Use Git-based workflows, CI/CD, automated testing, pull requests, and build and release pipelines with Azure DevOps and/or GitHub.
Design for security, identity, secrets management, logging, monitoring, resilience, scalability, and production support.
Collaborate with architecture, cybersecurity, data governance, infrastructure, and application teams.

Use AI tools with engineering judgment

Make effective use of GitHub Copilot, Claude, and similar assistants in day-to-day engineering.
Use AI tools to help create, refactor, debug, test, document, review, and maintain code.
Validate AI-generated code for correctness, security, performance, maintainability, and coding standards.
Look for ways to automate repetitive development and analysis work.

What you’ll bring

Professional experience in data engineering, analytics, machine learning, AI, or software engineering.
Strong Python and SQL skills.
Hands-on experience with Databricks, Spark/PySpark, and Delta Lake.
Experience designing and supporting production-scale ETL/ELT workflows and data pipelines.
Experience analyzing large, complex datasets.
Working knowledge of statistics and machine learning.
Experience developing solutions with LLMs and generative AI, including RAG, embeddings, vector search, prompt engineering, or evaluation.
Experience with Microsoft Azure.
A solid understanding of Git, CI/CD, DevOps, testing, code review, and production deployment.
Experience using AI coding assistants as part of software development.
The ability to take a business problem from early discovery through design, implementation, deployment, and production support.

Experience that’s a plus

Background in insurance, financial services, or another regulated, data-intensive industry.
Experience with property and casualty, commercial, specialty, or reinsurance data and processes.
Familiarity with underwriting, pricing, claims, customer or broker analytics, or document-based workflows.
Experience with Azure AI services, MLflow, MLOps, vector databases, or enterprise RAG architectures.
Experience building APIs and microservices for data and AI applications.
Familiarity with data governance, cataloging, lineage, model governance, and Responsible AI.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code and automated cloud deployments.
A degree in computer science, data science, artificial intelligence, engineering, mathematics, or a related field—or equivalent professional experience.

We’re now launching AI Labs - an incubator-style team operating like a startup within the company - to expand our reach and provide cutting-edge technical solutions to cities in areas beyond transit.

As a Staff Engineer
at Via, you'll be a founding member of Via's AI Labs. This is a rare opportunity to get in at the ground floor of something genuinely new: a dedicated space to move fast, experiment boldly, and build AI-powered products that could fundamentally change how Via and our partner cities operate. You'll have real autonomy, direct access to leadership, and the backing of a company that's already at scale - without the constraints that usually come with it. If you're experienced at building AI products end-to-end and you're energized by the idea of doing that with a blank canvas, this is the role for you.

About the Role:

Build and ship production-grade AI products end-to-end - owning everything from problem framing and data pipeline design through to deployment and iteration in live environments.
Work closely with our partners in a forward-deployed manner to deeply understand problems and constraints and iterate quickly on scalable agentic solutions.
Lead technical scoping workshops, directly interfacing with city leaders to solve challenging local problems with agentic workflows.
Work across a fast-moving and varied roadmap, contributing to intelligent tooling involving data consolidation, predictive modelling, real-time decision-making, and LLM-powered experiences.
Collaborate directly with product, data science, and operations teams to identify and prioritize the highest-impact AI opportunities across the business.
Write clean, scalable backend code that powers AI-driven features - designing APIs, managing data flows, and ensuring your systems perform reliably at scale.
Help shape the technical culture of AI Labs from the ground up - contributing to how the team builds, reviews, ships, and iterates.
Stay close to the frontier of AI development and bring new ideas, tools, and approaches into the team proactively.

About You:

You have 10+ years of hands-on experience building full stack applications and - with a track record of owning features end-to-end rather than working in isolation on models or research.
3+ years of working with AI tools and/or building AI powered products
You have deep expertise across the AI stack - including LLMs, predictive modelling, and the data infrastructure required to support them in real-world environments.
You're a strong engineer at your core - comfortable designing scalable APIs, working with distributed systems, and writing code that is clean, maintainable, and built to last.
You're energized by ambiguity and early-stage environments - you don't need everything to be defined to do great work, and you take ownership without being asked.

You thrive when working directly with users and customers, and are comfortable with travel to collaborate on-site.

Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI (Customer Agent)

About The Team

Our Engineering team builds the AI systems that power how brands run their businesses on Klaviyo. We move fast, ship in production, and hold a high bar for what "AI-native" actually means: systems that make real judgment calls, not demos.

The Customer Agent team is one of the newest and most ambitious groups in that org, based in Boston and working in-office: we're building a conversational AI system that lets brands serve their own customers at a scale no human support team could match. We're still small enough that one engineer’s work visibly shapes how the whole platform evolves. We're past the demo stage: the team ships changes against live customer traffic, measures quality with real evaluation frameworks, and treats reliability as a product feature, not an afterthought.

About The Role

Our team is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI to help build the future of Customer Agent, Klaviyo’s AI-native conversational platform. In this role, you’ll play a critical part in shaping how autonomous service, AI-driven support, and agentic commerce experiences evolve at scale across millions of customer interactions.

You’ll work across the stack to design, build, and scale systems that power intelligent workflows, conversational experiences, tools integrations, retrieval systems, onboarding flows, observability, and multi-channel customer engagement. You’ll help develop both foundational platform capabilities and customer-facing experiences that enable brands to launch, customize, and continuously improve their own highly-configurable AI agents.

As a Senior Engineer, you’ll tackle complex technical and product challenges, develop multiple solution paths, and evaluate business and architectural trade-offs to determine the best approach. You’ll also act as a technical leader and mentor, driving engineering quality, execution, and decision-making across projects. Additionally, you’ll be responsible for deploying well-designed, thoroughly tested solutions that prioritize reliability, scalability, and customer impact.

What We’re Looking For

A proven track record of building high-quality products and systems, with pride in writing clean, maintainable, high-quality code.
7+ years of experience in a software engineering role.
Strong experience developing end-to-end software solutions or extensive experience across both front-end and back-end technologies.
Experience building scalable, customer-facing systems in fast-moving product environments - we operate like a startup inside of Klaviyo.
Experience leading projects and being accountable for technical and business outcomes.
Experience mentoring team members or driving initiatives that help the team grow and learn new skills.
Experience conducting code reviews and maintaining a robust testing and deployment cycle.
Curiosity and enthusiasm for AI-native product development, including practical experience experimenting with LLMs, AI tooling, or agentic workflows in professional or personal projects.
Excitement about leveraging AI to improve engineering velocity, customer experiences, and operational workflows.
A strong product mindset and willingness to collaborate cross-functionally to solve ambiguous problems with urgency and pragmatism.

Job Description

Our artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) capabilities are critical accelerators of our mission to invent new medicines that save and improve lives. Core to the Data, AI, and Genome Sciences (DAGS) function is an AI/ML-first approach to improving target and biomarker discovery, validation, and selection, and elucidating complex disease mechanisms. As Senior Machine Learning Scientist, you will be responsible for developing and training large scale foundation models using biological data. Your work will advance our understanding of complex diseases and support the development of innovative therapeutic strategies. In this pursuit, you will have at your disposal high-performance clusters with several hundred state-of-the-art GPUs, access to biological, computational, and engineering experts from across our company and external vendors. You will be part of a broader, cross-functional team of computational biologists, data scientists, software engineers, and machine learning researchers who strive to identify therapeutic targets and biomarkers.

Design, develop, train, and implement novel ML algorithms particularly transformer-based foundation models for target discovery leveraging large scale biological data.
Collaborate with cross-functional team to identify research questions, data requirements, and develop appropriate, modern AI/ML solutions.

Strong expertise and experience in modern AI/ML approaches, training and working with large transformer-based models, representation learning, and related methodologies.
Experience with pre-training large scale models on multiple GPUs.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, and experience with standard deep learning frameworks like the PyTorch ecosystem
Interest in life sciences problems and disease biology, and willing to learn from and teach others.
Excellent communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in multi-disciplinary team.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer
at Via, you'll be a founding member of Via's new AI Labs - an incubator-style team operating like a startup within the company. This is a rare opportunity to get in at the ground floor of something genuinely new: a dedicated space to move fast, experiment boldly, and build AI-powered products that could fundamentally change how Via and our partner cities operate. You'll have real autonomy, direct access to leadership, and the backing of a company that's already at scale - without the constraints that usually come with it. If you're experienced at building AI products end-to-end and you're energized by the idea of doing that with a blank canvas, this is the role for you.

About the Role:

Build and ship production-grade AI products end-to-end - owning everything from problem framing and data pipeline design through to deployment and iteration in live environments.
Work closely with our customers in a forward-deployed manner to deeply understand problems and constraints and iterate quickly on scalable agentic solutions.

Stay close to the frontier of AI development and bring new ideas, tools, and approaches into the team proactively.

Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About The Role

Bedrock Robotics is hiring a Data Scientist to lead the work on Bedrock Intelligence, the product that turns data from construction machines into productivity metrics for our customers and our own teams. In this role, you will operate as a senior technical individual contributor, partnering closely with product, machine learning, backend, and customer-facing teams to extract insights from complex, real-world data generated by autonomous construction machines and their operators.

You will work across the full data science lifecycle (problem framing, analysis, measurement, and communication) while helping establish foundational practices for how data science is applied at Bedrock. This role is ideal for a senior-to-staff-level data scientist who enjoys operating in ambiguous problem spaces, working close to production systems and customers, and delivering insights that directly influence product and business decisions.

Collaborate closely with ML platform and data engineering teams to ensure data is accessible, reliable, and fit for analysis
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, influencing roadmap and design decisions
Contribute to the foundation of data science practices at Bedrock, helping shape how future work and teams scale
Build models when needed to forecast productivity, site throughput, or customer return on investment
Work with customers and commercial teams to turn their questions into analyses, recurring reports, and product features

First principles over inherited patterns

Auger was founded by Dave Clark and is backed by $150M from Oak HC/FT and Eclipse Capital. Our team works from Bellevue, WA and Dallas, TX.

About The AI Economics Team

We teach agentic systems to serve as any company’s economics and decision science team. Our work spans forecasting, causal inference, optimization, and the global intelligence these decisions require.

You will develop systems that combine global developments with a customer’s suppliers, products, orders, costs, and inventory; determine the business exposure; run the relevant models; and prepare or execute a coordinated response.

A tariff change, for example, requires more than identifying an affected supplier. The system must determine which purchases and products are exposed, calculate the financial impact, evaluate alternatives and their trade-offs, and assemble the actions required. It must present the evidence when a person needs to decide and execute when the customer has delegated that authority.

This is a hands-on role close to machine learning engineering. You will write production code, build data pipelines, program agents, and develop the tools and evaluation systems they need to work reliably. We are looking for an inventor and builder who can reason through an unfamiliar problem, develop an approach, and take responsibility for how it performs in production.

new_jobs.description:
Location:

Employment type:
Full-time

Head of AI/ML
Compensation:
$150,000 - $200,000

About SDI

SDI is a healthcare AI startup building surgical decision-support tools for spine surgery. Founded by practicing spine surgeons and academic faculty, we combine deep clinical expertise with modern machine learning to improve surgical planning and patient outcomes. Our platform spans medical imaging pipelines, clinical outcomes data, and ML models that operate on both.

The role

Our early research has found strong signals in spine MRI for predicting what happens to patients after imaging and after surgery. The job now is to build on that foundation: test the findings rigorously, extend them, and turn them into validated models running in our product. It needs to be done carefully enough that surgeons, journals and regulators will trust the results.

You’ll work closely with our clinical research lab, our founding surgeons and the AI/ML team. The problems range widely, from questions that need large-scale clinical data and careful study design to open methods problems in learning from 3D medical imaging. You’ll turn them into well-designed studies, models and code, and be able to tell when the data supports an answer and when it doesn’t. We expect you to go deep on the math when a problem calls for it, and to publish where it supports our goals.

Expect to spend roughly half your time on research and half on the engineering that makes it reproducible and shippable: building reproducible cohorts and training data, and writing training and evaluation code that others can run and build on. As our data foundations mature, the balance will shift toward research. On a team this small, research that can’t be reproduced or deployed doesn’t help anyone.

What you’ll work on

Problems on our roadmap include:

Outcomes and durability prediction.
Combine imaging features, segmentations and foundation-model embeddings with clinical and surgical data to predict how patients will do, including which patients are likely to need further treatment.
Representation learning for 3D MRI.
Self-supervised and foundation models for volumetric, multi-sequence spine MRI, where the anisotropy and multiple contrasts break assumptions built for 2D images.
Spatial prediction from imaging.
Predict where pathology and future events are likely, such as heat maps over the spine, not only whether they will occur.
Labels and expert disagreement.
Our labels come from radiologists and surgeons, and experts disagree. Model that disagreement, and decide which cases experts should label next.
Quantitative imaging biomarkers.
Make measurements comparable across scanners and sites: harmonization, test-retest agreement, and calibrated uncertainty.
Study design.
Build reproducible, leakage-free cohorts, and handle censoring, confounding and selection bias in real-world clinical data.
Learning across sites.
Models that keep adapting as new hospitals, scanners and pathologies come online, without forgetting what they’ve learned.
Evaluation and interpretability.
Evaluate models against the costs of real errors on ordinal grading scales, and test whether explanations of model behavior hold up.
Clinical NLP.
Extract and organize what’s in radiology reports, operative notes and clinic notes, and summarize a patient’s record into a concise spine health summary.

Engineering.
Write research code that others can run and extend. Track experiments and register models in MLflow. Work with the rest of the AI/ML team to move models from experiment to production in days rather than months. Publish where it supports our goals, in clinical spine journals and at venues like MICCAI, and contribute the research side of our FDA software-as-a-medical-device work.

What we’re looking for

A Ph.D. in a technical field such as machine learning, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology or biomedical engineering, with research focused on clinical or radiology problems. Ideally you’ve spent substantial time embedded in a clinical or radiology research group, working directly with real patient data and with physicians.
Hands-on experience building ML models on medical imaging, ideally MRI, in Python and PyTorch. You write the code yourself.
Statistical and mathematical depth. You’re comfortable with survival and time-to-event analysis, causal inference, and how to evaluate a model properly, and you can derive and reason about a method rather than only apply one.
Experience designing clinical studies or validation studies, and an understanding of why real-world clinical data misleads people.
Comfort working directly with physicians: you can understand their reasoning, challenge it constructively, and explain technical results in terms they can act on.
Software engineering habits: version control, tests, reproducible experiments, and code other people depend on.
A track record of research that reached the real world, through a product, a clinical tool, or work that others built on.

Nice to have

Musculoskeletal or spine imaging, or orthopedic or neurosurgical research.
Clinical NLP or LLMs applied to medical records: radiology reports, operative notes, information extraction and summarization.
Experience with inter-rater reliability, latent-variable label models, active learning or decision-curve analysis.
Representation learning and foundation models for medical imaging (e.g., DINO-style self-supervised learning).
MRI physics and harmonization across scanners and protocols.
Regulated medical software: FDA SaMD, clinical validation, HIPAA.
Peer-reviewed publications in clinical journals and in ML or medical imaging venues.

What this role is not

Not open-ended academic research. Publishing is encouraged, but the work has to make it into our product.
Not an MLOps or platform role. You’ll write code with production in mind and work closely with the team that ships it, but infrastructure and serving aren’t your job.
Not a role where you work alone on the clinical side. You’ll have strong clinical partners at HSS and on our advisory council. You won’t need to be the clinical expert, but you’ll need to speak their language.

new_jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, AI Agents
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About The Role

An AI agent is only as useful as what it knows about your company. For many of the world's leading companies, that knowledge lives in Notion. The AI Knowledge & Capabilities team makes sure every agent working in Notion – built by Notion, by customers, or by other AI companies – finds the right answer, quickly and at a cost that makes sense.

We own the systems that make this work: search, knowledge, and memory. We also own the agent harness – the tools, context, and model choices that turn a model into a working agent. We decide what to build using evals, customer feedback, and product judgment. Our work reaches users directly, and other AI teams at Notion build on it.

We recently shipped Memories, so Notion AI, Custom Agents, and agents connected through MCP can learn and remember across platforms. We also shipped Auto, a model router that delivers frontier quality at 90% lower cost. Next, we're bringing memory, search, and the harness together into one system. Nobody has figured out how to package that yet – we want any company to get a great knowledge system for its agents with a click or a few questions.

You will be a technical leader for the team. You'll set direction across search, knowledge, and the harness, starting hands-on with making agents better and cheaper, and help define how Notion measures AI quality.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

What You'll Achieve

Set technical direction for search, knowledge, and the agent harness – make the architecture calls, run design reviews, and decide what the team builds next.
Make Notion's agents better, faster, and cheaper – starting with the harness: which tools an agent can call, what context it gets, and which model handles each request.
Lead how we measure agent quality – evolve the metrics and evals that reflect real usage, and use them to choose what ships.
Turn company data into answers agents can use – build agentic search and memory that give every agent the context it needs, at the right latency and cost.
Work closely with research – partner with Notion's model research team on evals, model choice, and models trained for agentic work, and get what works into production. You'll also work with search platform and AI product teams on work that spans teams.
Grow the team – mentor engineers, review designs, and develop the next tech leads.

Skills You'll Need To Bring

Production applied AI: You've shipped and iterated on production LLM or agent systems used by real users. You owned how their quality was measured, and you changed course based on what you found.
Quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs: You've traded quality against latency and cost in a production system, measured the result, and can explain what you gave up and why.
Technical leadership: You've owned the technical direction of a complex system, often across teams, and kept it sound as it grew. You don't wait for a roadmap – you find the problems worth solving, make the case for them, and go deep on the hardest ones yourself.
Product sense: You've shipped quality improvements users noticed, and you've shaped new products from scratch – from the data model to what users see. You can explain why they mattered.
Shipping something new: You've taken an idea from nothing to a product people use. You try new models and tools early, form your own views, and turn them into product decisions.
Making other engineers better: You mentor engineers at every level, guide their designs, and share what you know so it scales past you. Multiple engineers have grown by working with you.
Clear communication: You write clearly about tradeoffs, disagree directly, and change your mind when the evidence says to.

Nice To Haves

You've improved LLM cost and quality directly – e.g. model routing, eval-driven harness or prompt tuning, or token efficiency in long-running agents.
You've founded a company or been an early engineer at a startup, and built systems that hold up at large scale.
Experience working closely with research or model training teams.

You will be responsible for developing and implementing cutting-edge artificial intelligence solutions that drive innovation and enhance performance. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams and leverage your expertise in machine learning, deep learning, and data analysis to solve complex problems and deliver impactful AI-driven solutions.

Position Responsibilities

Collaborate with stakeholders to engineer innovative solutions for new system roll-outs, enhancements, and maintenance of existing applications, ensuring adherence to programming standards.
Develop system specifications, create test plans, and conduct project and issue management for the assigned scope of work.
Design/Build solutions using AI services and machine learning models to address unique use cases, employing cutting-edge techniques and methodologies.
Utilize machine learning and advanced AI techniques to extract valuable insights from complex datasets and solve intricate problems.
Deploy trained models into production environments, ensuring scalability, reliability, and optimal performance, while integrating seamlessly with existing systems and applications.
Design and implement agents and multi-agent architectures to optimize client workflows.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Minimum of 3 years of full-time experience in Data Analysis, Statistics, Machine Learning, or Computer Science
Minimum of 2 years of experience in machine learning, deep learning, or demonstrated proficiency in Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Minimum of 2 years of experience with AI/ML and cognitive services provided by at least one cloud service provider
Minimum of 1 year of experience in building Conversational AI applications using cloud-based services and in orchestrating AI/ML services for building a complete solution
Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience)

Bonus Points If You Have

Hands-on involvement with speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and chatbot technologies

new_jobs.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Sonalysts, Inc. is seeking a highly skilled Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Systems Engineer
with deep expertise in

Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Generative AI, AI agents, and Model Context Protocol
.

The ideal candidate should have experience in designing, developing, and optimizing AI-powered applications and workflows with a strong foundation in cybersecurity best practices
.

Who are we?

Sonalysts, Inc. is a small, 100% employee-owned business (ESOP) that supports a very diverse set of customers. While the company was originally founded in 1973 with a focus on sonar analysis for the Navy (hence the name), Sonalysts has since expanded into a variety of other Defense and Commercial spaces. With current contracts supporting the Navy, Air Force, Army, and many other customers, Sonalysts leverages the skills and knowledge of its employee owners to help solve the Department of Defense’s most challenging problems while providing the best benefit to our customers. Sonalysts has a diverse and capable workforce comprised of former and retired service members from all branches of the military, and professionals with a wide range of commercial and technical backgrounds. From software development to operations analysis, doctrinal development, engineering, wargaming, targeted knowledge elicitation, or large group facilitation, Sonalysts can meet any challenge.

A small, central corporate structure coupled with a largely de-centralized approach to project management enables Sonalysts to compete with larger Defense Contractors in providing rapid, innovative solutions to meet customer needs while remaining agile and entrepreneurial at heart. Our employee-owners lead and support existing projects while also developing new business and winning new work.

If you are looking to use your technical knowledge to solve challenging problems for the military while benefiting from the flexibility and empowerment of being a contractor or potential future leader in a small business, then Sonalysts may be the place for you.

Key Responsibilities

Design and implement scalable LLM-based architectures for AI-powered applications.
Develop and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines for improved model accuracy.
Work with Generative AI models to enhance automated decision-making systems.
Integrate and deploy AI models using AI Agents, Model Context Protocol, and retrieval strategies.
Develop automation workflows using N8N, Pydantic, or other AI workflow tools.
Optimize and fine-tune AI/ML models for performance and efficiency.
Utilize GPU acceleration and frameworks like TensorFlow, PyTorch for large-scale AI workloads.
Implement secure coding practices and cybersecurity protocols in all AI/ML development workflows.
Ensure secure data handling, model access control, and compliance with data privacy regulations.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate AI solutions into production environments.
Research and implement state-of-the-art advancements in LLMs, multimodal AI, and generative systems.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Must be a U.S. citizen, eligible for a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) SECRET security clearance*
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, or a related field.
3 or more years of professional experience that includes developing and integrating LLMs, RAG, and Generative AI based solutions.
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work in fast-paced, AI-driven environments.

Desired Experience

US Navy Combat Systems Proven experience working with US Navy combat systems, specifically applying systems engineering and software development principles to mission-critical defense environments.
Containerization & Orchestration Deep technical proficiency in software containerization technologies, including Docker, Kubernetes, and OpenShift, for the deployment and scaling of complex software architectures.
Experience with vector databases, knowledge retrieval strategies, and fine-tuning AI models.
Knowledge of cloud-based AI deployment (AWS, GCP, Azure) with secure infrastructure practices.
Familiarity with open-source AI tools and frameworks for custom AI solution development.
Knowledge of compliance standards such as DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF), NIST, and ISO/IEC 27000 series.
Contributions to AI research, publications, or open-source projects are a plus.
Strong background in Python, AI frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch), and GPU architectures for model training/inference.
Experience with AI Agent frameworks and Model Context Protocol for scalable AI solutions.
Hands-on experience with N8N, Pydantic, or other AI workflow tools.
Demonstrated experience implementing cybersecurity controls in AI environments (e.g., secure APIs, authentication/authorization, encryption).
Familiarity with threat modeling, vulnerability assessment, and secure deployment of AI models.
Deep understanding of retrieval systems, knowledge graphs, and multimodal AI applications.

What’s in it for you?

Opportunity to provide important support to the DoD and to expand your work portfolio to support various projects across the company.
Opportunity to grow your skillset and pursue project leadership.
Salary ranges between $85,000-$130,000, dependent on experience, qualifications and other relevant business criteria.
Becoming an integral part of an innovative employee-owned company which includes
Flexible Time Program enabling an optimal work-life balance by permitting partners to arrange their work around personal appointments and vacations, parent-teacher conferences, children’s activities and the like, so long as the partner gets the job done on time.
Paid Time Off
401(k) Plan with company match
Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
Sales Bonus Program
Special Performance and Retention Bonus Program
Health and Preventive Dental Insurance
Dependent Care Assistance Plan
Health Care Reimbursement Plan
Employee Referral Bonus Program
Professional Development (e.g. Tuition Reimbursement Program, Online Training Program, and Targeted Skills Program)
Relocation Assistance
Obtaining a U.S. Government security clearance involves a comprehensive background check. Candidates are eligible for a clearance if they have demonstrated sound financial management (including good credit) over time, are free of criminal records, have limited foreign contacts or ties, and other factors indicative of a position of trust to protect information sensitive to the U.S. Government.

Sonalysts, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, and will not be discriminated against on the basis of, race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, disability, or other basis protected by law.

This job is not available to residents of New York City because of local law restrictions there.

new_jobs.title: AI Engineering Lead
new_jobs.description:
Building the people that build the world.

With platforms in HVAC and Detection and Measurement, SPX Technologies builds innovative solutions that enable a safer, more efficient, sustainable world. Through our RiSE talent development framework, we Reach, Identify, Strengthen, and Engage our employees to support them in their continued development. We’re a global company of problem solvers, collaborators, and innovators, and our businesses build solutions that impact the world.

How You Will Make An Impact (Job Summary)

SPX is a diverse team of unique individuals who all make an impact. As an Enterprise AI Engineering Lead, you will define and build the generative and agentic AI architecture supporting our business segments and corporate functions. You will establish enterprise standards and guardrails, develop production-grade reference implementations, and advise business and technology leaders to turn AI opportunities into secure, governed, measurable business outcomes.

What You Can Expect In This Role (Job Responsibilities)

While each day brings new opportunities at SPX, your core responsibilities will be:

AI Strategy & Enterprise Architecture

Own the blueprint. Define the enterprise AI reference architecture — LLM and agent platforms, RAG, orchestration, integration patterns, reusable components and deployment standards — with build-vs-buy guidance.
Set the roadmap. Create a pragmatic 12–24 month AI architecture roadmap aligned to SPX business priorities and our Azure-first cloud and Microsoft Fabric data landscape.
Set the standards. Establish guidance for model selection, prompt and agent design, evaluation, and cost and performance management across AI platforms (Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry, Anthropic Claude, Copilot ecosystem).

Hands-on Build & Delivery

Build, not just draw. Design and build reusable agentic AI components, accelerators and reference solutions: multi-agent workflows, RAG pipelines, tool/function calling, MCP and agent-to-agent integration patterns, memory management, and copilots — including AI-driven user experiences and, where valuable, generative UI.
Ship to production. Lead proofs of concept and take the successful ones to production with delivery teams and partners.
Raise the bar. Lead architecture, design and code reviews, and guide internal engineers and partner teams through delivery.

Governance, Security & Responsible AI

Make it operable. Establish LLMOps and observability practices: CI/CD, evaluation, monitoring, guardrails, and cost tracking for AI workloads.
Make it safe. Partner with Security, Legal, Privacy and Compliance to implement responsible AI: data access controls, IP protection, model risk, bias testing, and human-in-the-loop controls.
Make it data-ready. Define data readiness and integration requirements with data and platform teams across ERP, CRM, PLM, IoT/OT and document repositories, anchored on Microsoft Fabric as the enterprise data platform.

Business & Executive Engagement

Advise the business. Translate segment and functional business problems into AI solution designs and clear value cases, and present architecture decisions, trade-offs and progress up to the executive level.
Guide the ecosystem. Support vendor, hyperscaler and partner evaluations, including technical due diligence.
Scan the horizon. Track emerging technology (agent frameworks, MCP/A2A-style protocols, small and fine-tuned models, multimodal) and recommend adoption where it adds value.

Enablement & Technical Leadership

Multiply others. Mentor developers, data engineers and solution architects, and raise AI literacy across IT and the business.
Lead by influence. Lead through influence across a virtual team of IT, data, security and business partners — without direct authority.

What we are looking for (Experience, Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, Education)

We each bring something to the table, and we are looking for someone who has:

Required Experience

10+ years in software, data or solution architecture, with 3+ years building production Generative AI / Agentic AI solutions.
Demonstrated hands-on delivery of LLM applications, agentic and multi-agent systems, and RAG, using frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel or similar — including MCP, tool/function calling, prompt engineering, memory management and AI guardrails.
Strong Python and API development (FastAPI or similar), plus experience with vector databases, search and retrieval, microservices, Docker, Kubernetes and CI/CD.
Hands-on experience on a major cloud AI platform — Azure preferred (Azure OpenAI, AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, AKS, Functions); AWS (Bedrock) or GCP (Vertex AI) also valued.
At least one enterprise-scale AI or data platform taken from concept to production, with measurable business results.
Working knowledge of enterprise security, identity, data governance and compliance for AI.
Proven ability to communicate with executives and non-technical stakeholders, with practical delivery skills: scoping, roadmapping, estimation, dependency management, and working with PMs and delivery teams.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Experience in manufacturing, industrial, HVAC, engineering or IoT/OT environments.
Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform and the Copilot ecosystem, and enterprise systems integration (SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, Teams, SharePoint).
Fine-tuning, small language models, or model evaluation experience (PyTorch, Hugging Face or similar); React/TypeScript for AI front ends.
Experience mentoring or leading small technical teams (5–10) or cross-functional initiatives.
Patents, publications or public technical contributions (a plus, not required).

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree required; Master's in Computer Science, AI/ML, Engineering or a related field preferred.
Cloud or AI architecture certifications (Azure, AWS or equivalent).

Travel & Working Environment

Hybrid schedule of three days onsite per week
Occasional travel to business segment sites

How We Live Our Culture

Our culture is at the center of what we do and, more importantly, who we are. Our core values set a standard for how we manage ourselves, and our Leadership Model sets the standard for how we engage with each other. Whether you are an individual contributor or you lead a large team, each of us leads at SPX.

What benefits do we offer?

We know that the well-being of our employees is integral. Our benefits include:

Generous and flexible paid time off including paid personal time off, caregiver, parental, and volunteer leave
Competitive health insurance plans and 401(k) match, with benefits starting day one
Competitive and performance-based compensation packages and bonus plans
Educational assistance, leadership development programs, and recognition programs

Our commitment to embrace diversity to build a culture of inclusion at SPX

We value different backgrounds, experiences, and voices at SPX, and we are committed to challenging ourselves, openly communicating, and striving to improve every day. We believe in creating an inclusive work environment where everyone has a voice and is encouraged to realize their fullest potential.

new_jobs.description:
We understand that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today, and that’s why we’re inspired to make A Better World for Pets. Antech is comprised of a diverse team of individuals who are committed to each other’s growth and development. Our culture is centered on our guiding philosophy, The Five Principles: Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom. Today Antech is driving the future of pet health as part of Mars Science & Diagnostics, a family-owned company focused on veterinary care.

Current Associates will need to apply through the internal career site. Please log into Workday and click on Menu or View All Apps, select the Jobs Hub app, then click the magnifying glass to Browse Jobs.

The Target Pay Range for this position is $103,000- $129,000 annually. At Mars Science and Diagnostics, pay decisions are determined using factors such as relevant job-related skills, experience, education, training and budget.

Working within the Next Generation Technologies team at Mars Science & Diagnostics, this unique role sits at the intersection of veterinary medicine and artificial intelligence. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine with a strong foundation in Data Science. In this role, you will bring unique value by leveraging both your medical and technical backgrounds to solve complex AI problems. Acting as a crucial bridge between clinical experts (DVMs, radiologists, oncologists) and technical teams, you will provide domain leadership while delivering hands-on technical data science work. You will also manage key segments of our AI product portfolio, starting with advanced CT modality innovations, under the guidance of the AI Director.

What are we looking for?

Education & Domain Expertise: A Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree (or near completion) combined with formal studies, degree, or strong proven experience in Data Science, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
Technical & Clinical Fluency: Savviness in the technical AI domain with the ability to "speak the language" of both data scientists and clinical specialists (radiologists, oncologists).
Project Management Skills: Capable of managing projects within a large product portfolio creation, with an initial focus on CT imaging modalities.
Key Behavioral Competencies: Tech Savvy, Being Resilient, Nimble Learning, Action Oriented, Collaborates, Drives Results, Customer Focus.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Technical & Clinical Liaison: Act as the primary conduit between the technical AI development side and the medical/clinical side, ensuring that our AI models address real-world veterinary needs and are clinically sound.
Hands-on AI Delivery: Execute data science tasks, actively building, training, and refining AI models and algorithms specific to the Mars Science and Diagnostics domain.
Project Management: Oversee and manage a sizable portion of a large AI product portfolio creation. Initially focused on our CT modality projects, this responsibility will expand to encompass additional activities under the guidance of your manager.
Dual-Domain Leadership: Provide technical and medical thought leadership within your scope, combining clinical intuition with data-driven insights to push the boundaries of next-generation veterinary diagnostic tools.

What can you expect from Mars?

Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose-driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

About Antech

Antech is a leader in veterinary diagnostics, driven by our passion for innovation that delivers better animal health outcomes. Our products and services span 90+ reference laboratories around the globe; in-house diagnostic laboratory instruments and consumables, including rapid assay diagnostic products and digital cytology services; local and cloud-based data services; practice information management software and related software and support; veterinary imaging and technology; veterinary professional education and training; and board-certified specialist support services.

Benefits

Antech offers an industry competitive benefits package and continues to invest in and evolve benefits programs that meet the health, wellness and financial needs of our associates.

Benefits eligiblity is based on employment status.

Paid Time Off & Holidays
Medical, Dental, Vision (Multiple Plans Available)
Basic Life (Company Paid) & Supplemental Life
Short and Long Term Disability (Company Paid)
Flexible Spending Accounts/Health Savings Accounts
Paid Parental Leave
401(k) with company match
Tuition/Continuing Education Reimbursement
Life Assistance Program
Pet Care Discounts

Commitment to Equal Employer Opportunities

new_jobs.title: Applied Scientist II, Brand Optimization
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing businesses, responsible for defining and delivering a collection of advertising products that drive discovery and sales. Brand advertising is at the center of that growth, and brand marketers are pushing the industry toward a fundamental shift: they no longer want to optimize toward proxy metrics like reach and frequency alone. They want their investment across Streaming TV, online video, and display to drive measurable business outcomes, from consideration through to purchase and long-term loyalty. The core scientific challenge is connecting a brand ad exposure today to an outcome that may happen days or weeks later, and then optimizing for it in real time.

The Brand Outcomes Optimization team exists to solve that challenge. We build machine-learned models that predict how likely a customer is to move along the full funnel, from awareness through conversion, and we integrate those predictions into real-time bidding so that every brand bid is placed on the opportunity most likely to produce the outcome the advertiser cares about. These systems operate at large scale, and even small improvements to how we predict and optimize for outcomes have meaningful and immediate impact on advertiser results.

As an Applied Scientist II, you will help drive this outcome-optimization. You will take on increasingly ambiguous problems, from predicting what a brand outcome will be, to building the bidding and control algorithms that optimize for it, to proving the lift through experimentation. You will work alongside senior scientists and engineers, applying advances in machine learning, online optimization, optimal control, forecasting, and causal inference. You will also join the Amazon science community, with opportunities to publish papers, attend workshops and conferences, and gain early access to Amazon ML technologies.

Key job responsibilities

Role

In this role, you will work with a highly motivated team of ML scientists and engineers focused on making brand advertising measurable and optimizable against real outcomes. As an Applied Scientist II, you will:

Contribute to outcome-driven brand optimization, helping define, predict, and bid toward brand outcomes across channels.
Build prediction models that estimate a customer's likelihood to progress through the funnel, and integrate them into bidding systems.
Develop the optimization and control algorithms that turn outcome predictions into bids.
Own projects end to end: frame the problem and success metrics, build and validate prototypes, partner with engineers to productionize, and prove impact through offline analysis and online A/B experimentation.
Help establish scalable, automated processes for training, monitoring, and feedback so outcome optimization stays reliable and performant at scale.
Contribute to the science bar on the team through design and model reviews.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of building models for business application experience
PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience in designing experiments and statistical analysis of results

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in state-of-the-art deep learning models architecture design and deep learning training and optimization and model pruning

new_jobs.description:
About Ayo

We are a venture-backed early-stage startup developing processors specialized for machine learning. The processor will provide orders of magnitude improvement in speed and power efficiency with a goal of unseating the GPU as the dominant computing platform for machine learning.

The Role

We're looking for a hands-on machine learning engineer to join our founding team and get models running on our photonic processor. You'll take models from PyTorch to prototype silicon and digital twins, figure out what breaks, fix it, and feed what you learn straight back to the hardware team. This is a builder role: you'll own real problems end to end, move fast, and work shoulder to shoulder with photonics, ASIC, and FPGA engineers who are building something no one has built before.

No prior hardware experience required. If you're early in your career, fresh out of a PhD, and itching to work on something genuinely new, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Partner with our engineering teams to train models that run successfully on Ayo chips
Deploy and run trained models on our prototype hardware and digital twins, and turn them into working demonstrations on our chips
Build and adapt training and inference pipelines for a compute environment that doesn't behave like a GPU
Work directly with hardware engineers to test ideas, find bottlenecks, and shape the processor architecture with what you learn
Build the tooling, benchmarks, and software infrastructure our machine learning work runs on
Help show the world what Ayo's processor can do by supporting demos and go-to-market work

What We're Looking For

PhD or MS in machine learning, computer science, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field (recent grads welcome), or equivalent hands-on experience
Has built and trained neural networks from scratch, and understands how they work under the hood
Full-stack ML engineering skills: data pipelines, training, evaluation, and deployment
Fluent in Python and PyTorch (TensorFlow or JAX also welcome)
A bias toward action: you'd rather ship a working prototype than perfect a plan
Excitement about novel hardware. You don't need photonics or silicon experience, just curiosity and the drive to learn fast

Nice to Have

Experience with distributed training or large-scale compute
Model optimization experience such as quantization, pruning, compilers, or custom kernels (CUDA, Triton)
Interpretability or explainability work
Any exposure to hardware, FPGAs, or analog or in-memory compute

Why Ayo

You'll be a founding machine learning team member, shaping how we deploy machine learning on an entirely new kind of processor.
We are working on a genuinely hard and interesting problem: unseating the GPU as the dominant machine learning compute platform.
Early-stage means real ownership, real impact, and meaningful equity.
Competitive salary. Equity commensurate with stage and seniority. Benefits package including health, dental, and vision.
Fully onsite in Boston - we are a collaborative, in-person team.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Researcher
new_jobs.description:
About Ayo

We are a venture-backed early-stage startup developing processors specialized for machine learning. The processor will provide orders of magnitude improvement in speed and power efficiency with a goal of unseating the GPU as the dominant computing platform for machine learning.

The Role

We're looking for a hands-on machine learning researcher to join our founding team and get models running on our photonic processor. You'll take models from PyTorch to prototype silicon and digital twins, figure out what breaks, fix it, and feed what you learn straight back to the hardware team. This is a builder role: you'll own real problems end to end, move fast, and work shoulder to shoulder with photonics, ASIC, and FPGA engineers who are building something no one has built before.

No prior hardware experience required. If you're early in your career, fresh out of a PhD, and itching to work on something genuinely new, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Partner with our engineering teams to train models that run successfully on Ayo chips
Deploy and run trained models on our prototype hardware and digital twins, and turn them into working demonstrations on our chips
Build and adapt training and inference pipelines for a compute environment that doesn't behave like a GPU
Work directly with hardware engineers to test ideas, find bottlenecks, and shape the processor architecture with what you learn
Build the tooling, benchmarks, and software infrastructure our machine learning work runs on
Help show the world what Ayo's processor can do by supporting demos and go-to-market work

What We're Looking For

PhD or MS in machine learning, computer science, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field (recent grads welcome), or equivalent hands-on experience
Has built and trained neural networks from scratch, and understands how they work under the hood
Full-stack ML engineering skills: data pipelines, training, evaluation, and deployment
Fluent in Python and PyTorch (TensorFlow or JAX also welcome)
A bias toward action: you'd rather ship a working prototype than perfect a plan
Excitement about novel hardware. You don't need photonics or silicon experience, just curiosity and the drive to learn fast

Nice to Have

Experience with distributed training or large-scale compute
Model optimization experience such as quantization, pruning, compilers, or custom kernels (CUDA, Triton)
Interpretability or explainability work
Any exposure to hardware, FPGAs, or analog or in-memory compute

Why Ayo

You'll be a founding machine learning team member, shaping how we deploy machine learning on an entirely new kind of processor.
We are working on a genuinely hard and interesting problem: unseating the GPU as the dominant machine learning compute platform.
Early-stage means real ownership, real impact, and meaningful equity.
Competitive salary. Equity commensurate with stage and seniority. Benefits package including health, dental, and vision.
Fully onsite in Boston - we are a collaborative, in-person team.

Healthcare is complex. We’re here to change that.

RVO Health is a health technology company on a mission to make health easier to navigate, more accessible, and more affordable for everyone.

Here, you'll help over 40 million people every month, with a team that genuinely cares about the work and each other.

At a Glance

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help build AI-powered tools that will accelerate and improve our internal operations. This role requires experience owning backend systems, APIs, production architecture, and AI Evaluations.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role at the center of a growing AI Ops function within Corporate Technology. You will design and build solutions that automate real workflows, integrate with enterprise tools, and are grounded in sound software engineering practices.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working across the full AI development stack: from designing and fine tuning AI workflows to building APIs and integrating third-party platforms. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-moving environment, can translate a business workflow into a technical architecture, and cares about delivering work that is reliable, maintainable, and secure.

This role reports into the Director of Data Science and works closely with the AI Ops team, security, IT, and platform engineering. It is an early and influential seat in a program that will accelerate the adoption and use of AI across RVO Health.

Where You'll Be

Location: Minneapolis, MN | Hybrid

We believe great collaboration happens when we're together, solving problems, learning from each other, and connecting as a team. That's why we’re in our offices Tuesday through Thursday each week. You are welcome to work remotely Mondays and Fridays if you wish.

Address: 11000 Optum Cir Eden Prairie, MN 55344

What You’ll Do

Design, build, and iterate on AI agents integrated with enterprise tools including Outlook, Slack, and internal data sources
Develop and maintain evaluation pipelines and feedback loops to continuously improve quality and reliability
Build and maintain APIs, backend services, and integrations that connect AI capabilities to the tools teams already use
Collaborate with AI Ops, security, IT, and platform engineering teams to ensure systems are production-grade, secure, and observable
Contribute to a repeatable framework for building new AI Assistants as the program expands
Enable the organization by building a marketplace of shared skills/plugins
Evaluate new models, tools, and libraries and make informed recommendations on when and how to adopt them
Identify and mitigate risks related to AI outputs, data handling, and responsible use
Contribute to technical documentation, runbooks, and onboarding materials that help the team scale what gets built

What We’re Looking For

3+ years of data science or engineering experience, with at least 1 year focused on building LLM-powered applications
Experience building and deploying apps in cloud infrastructure
Experience integrating with third-party APIs and enterprise tools (Jira, Slack, or similar platforms is a plus)
Experience with software engineering best practices including: version control, testing, CI/CD, observability, and code review
Strong communication skills and the ability to work with non-technical stakeholders to understand workflows and translate them into technical requirements

new_jobs.title: AI Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) organization helps Stripe's most strategic customers design and validate technical solutions that drive their business forward. Within SA, our team builds the tools, workflows, and custom technical assets that make the broader SA org more effective—turning individual ingenuity into org-wide capability.

We are looking for AI Engineers who are energized by working close to the business and the users we serve. You'll operate as an embedded, high-context engineer focused on the highest-leverage opportunities across the SA org—building production-quality tooling, supporting our most strategic engagements, and shipping automation that meaningfully improves how Solutions Architects work every day.

What You'll Do

As an AI Engineer, you'll be embedded directly with the Solutions Architecture team—building alongside them, deeply understanding their workflows, and shipping tools and automation that permanently change how they operate. Your measure of success is SA productivity: the engagements you've accelerated, the workflows you've transformed, and the tools you've built that the org adopts as default.

You'll ship code daily. You'll discover where SAs lose time and build high-impact solutions. You'll take what works for one person and scale it to work for the org. And when our most strategic customer engagements need custom technical assets, you'll build those too.

This is a role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of engineering and business impact—close to customers, close to revenue, and building for people you can see using your work every day.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solutions Architects, SA leadership, Product, and Engineering to scope technical work and translate ambiguous business needs into well-defined deliverables
Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities (LLMs, agents, workflow automation) where they provide genuine leverage—not for novelty, but for measurable productivity improvement
Architect and build internal tools, agents, and automated workflows that accelerate SA and manager productivity across technical discovery, solution design, demoing, user engagements, territory/pipeline management, and product interlock
Take high-potential tools and workflows built by SAs and managers and harden them into scalable, maintainable, production-grade solutions
Identify patterns across SA workflows and proactively build solutions that address recurring friction
Build custom demo environments, PoC applications, and technical assets for Stripe's most strategic customer engagements
Document tools, architectures, and usage patterns so others can adopt and extend what you've built
Debug, extend, and maintain backend systems across a variety of codebases and infrastructure

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience as an engineer shipping production systems
Strong backend engineering fundamentals: you can debug a failing system, trace issues across services, and reason about data flows
Experience building and deploying AI agents, LLM-powered tools, or workflow automation beyond basic prompt engineering
Experience scoping and delivering work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment
Proficiency in at least two of: Ruby, Node.js, Python, or Next.js
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) including deployment, monitoring, and basic DevOps
Experience building internal tools, developer platforms, or workflow automation
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context

Who You Are

Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:

You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $172,600 - $258,800. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Genuine enthusiasm for client-facing, services-oriented work, and a preference for delivering solutions to clients over building a product

Demonstrated experience with agentic systems: ability to show what you have built, explain where it failed, and describe how you fixed it
